ranking.reason: Kept at rank 1. The external BATFET carries the pack current, and charge current is sensed at the cells. Charge voltage steps are 8 mV. It uses I2C at 6Bh, and the firmware-identical alternate BQ25703ARSNR passes rule 4. None of P3's finds beats it on a requirement value.
Kept at rank 2. Same circuit and I2C address as rank 1, with 16 mV charge-voltage steps (8400 mV is still exact) and no pass-through mode. It is rank 1's rule-5 alternate.

Same NVDC circuit and 8 mV steps as rank 1. It uses SMBus at 09h, so it is not firmware-identical to ranks 1 and 2. JLCPCB holds 1857 of it, against 71 of the BQ25713BRSNR, so it ranks above that part. SLUSD20B gives the BQ25700A as its pin-to-pin and software-compatible partner.
The SMBus counterpart of rank 2: same circuit, 16 mV steps, SMBus at 09h. JLCPCB 1680, Digi-Key 7182.
Moved from rank 3 to rank 5. Same function as rank 1 at I2C address 6Ah. JLCPCB stock of 71 barely clears the gate of 50, so it ranks below the SMBus pair, which has 1857 and 1680.

Meets every Pack charger value, but it has no BATFET (SLUSE66A Device Comparison Table: 'BATFET Power Path No'). It therefore does not cover the Power path function, and the board would still need a separate power-path part. It also costs more than ranks 1 to 5 (3.0231 at 1 piece).

Qualifies, because the ILIMIT pin does scale the input limit (see dropped reason refuted in report). It ranks last for three reasons. First, the inductor current limit is 45 to 60 mV across the sense resistor, so holding 3.0 A at the maximum leaves 2.25 A at the minimum. Second, it costs 14.2234 at 1 piece, against 2.4269 for rank 1. Third, Digi-Key's lead time is 49 weeks. It is the only candidate that charges with no firmware, since it has no I2C and no watchdog.

ranking.reason: Kept at rank 1. It presents dead-battery Rd, runs from VBUS over 2.85 to 5.5 V, and its GPIO outputs set the charger's ILIM_HIZ with no firmware. Its 2.85 V minimum leaves the most margin for VBUS droop under a 3 A draw; the droop itself is not stated in the tree.

Same role as rank 1 with no firmware. It is set to UFP by the PORT pin, reports Default, 1.5 A or 3.0 A on the open-drain OUT1/OUT2 pins, has RCC_DB of 4.1 to 6.1 kOhm, and runs at -40 to 85 degC. It ranks below rank 1 because its VDD minimum is 4.5 V, against 2.85 V.
Same pins and function as rank 2. TA is 0 to 70 degC, which covers 0 to 50 degC with less margin. Its data sheet gives dead-battery Rd in text only, with no RCC_DB figure.

Firmware-free in GPIO mode, with UFP set by the PORT pin and RCC_DB of 4.1 to 6.1 kOhm. Its VDD is 2.7 to 5 V, so it cannot sit on 5.5 V VBUS and needs the 3.3 V rail or an LDO. Its non-failsafe pins can back-drive it when VDD is off.
Same as rank 4 and -40 to 85 degC. Digi-Key holds 0, so its second source is the pin-matched TUSB320LIRWBR in GPIO mode.
Moved from rank 2. The input limit reaches the charger only through firmware over I2C. It is a PD controller, larger and dearer than ranks 1 to 5.
It powers up in Sink mode with interrupts masked, and BC_LVL reports the advertisement over I2C with INT_N. Firmware passes the limit to the charger. JLCPCB 10325.
Moved from rank 3. I2C only. Every change of the limit needs firmware.

GPIO mode is dual-role only; 'UFP-only mode is not available in GPIO mode' (SLLSEO5D 6.3.2). On this sink-only port it therefore needs I2C mode and a firmware write of MODE_SELECT after every EN_N or soft reset.

It writes the BQ25713's input limit itself over its I2C controller port, with no RP2354B firmware in the path. At boot, though, it needs a configuration and patch from an external I2C EEPROM of at least 36 kB at 0x50, which is not selected, or from a host. It also takes the charger onto its own controller bus beside the RP2354B's watchdog writes.

report.value: P2's V153 places R5's floor disconnect between VSYS and the board's loads. With it open, the loads lose supply while USB-C is present. That contradicts V152's USB-only operation unless R5 reconnects on charger presence. A CC detector on the 3.3 V rail (TUSB320I or TUSB320LI) and the RP2354B's charger watchdog writes also depend on that rail. It is for R5 and P5 to settle
report.source: P2's return, V152 and V153; SLUSD83C 9.3.10.1 watchdog as quoted there
